transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah... I came in because I can’t stop getting startled. Like, if a breaker snaps, or a tool drops, or somebody walks up behind me, I jump hard—like I’m coming out of my skin. And then my heart just keeps pounding way after everyone else has already moved on.
Do these startle reactions remind you of any specific past events that were scary or traumatic for you?

Yeah. It’s tied to that thing that happened. Sometimes out of nowhere I’ll see the flash in my head, or I’ll hear the trainee yelling again. I could just be loading tools in the truck, nothing going on, and it hits me like I’m right back there. It really knocks me sideways.
Do you find yourself constantly on guard, like you’re always watching for danger, even in places you know are safe?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I notice the jumping at sounds more than anything. I don’t know if I’m always watching for danger exactly… I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Have you been avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of what happened?

Yeah. I do. I’ll make excuses so I don’t have to go near certain panels or breakers, or certain job sites that feel too close to what happened. And I don’t really like talking about that day either, because once it gets going in my head, I can’t shut it off.
Since that day, do you find yourself feeling angry, fearful, or guilty a lot of the time, even when there’s no immediate danger or reminder around?

Yeah… a lot. I’m angry most of the time, even when nothing’s happening. And guilty. I keep feeling like I failed that kid, like I should’ve done something different. It’s like I’m carrying it around all day, and I feel like everybody can see it on me.
